newsitem.title: FINLAND: CULTOR WARNS AGAINST HIGH PROFIT HOPES.
newsitem.headline: CULTOR WARNS AGAINST HIGH PROFIT HOPES.

text.p: Finnish food and biotechnology group Cultor Oy said on Monday it had warned share analysts about overly high expectations of its results, and that its first six months had been weaker than estimated.
"We want to cut the wings of too high result expectations," CEO Bjorn Mattson said in a statement, without specifying which period he referred to.

Cultor said in the statement -- which summarised its comments to analysts -- that its preliminary eight-month figures showed the first six months were "lower than estimated" but July-August were "substantially better".
"Our view has been that Cultor's result for the entire year will be somewhat lower than last year," he said.
Cultor last said in June it expected this year's profits to be at about last year's level.
Its 1995 profit after financial items was 491 million markka and its earnings per share were 14.91 markka.
"During the first months of the year the results were affected by high raw-material prices and problems with raw-material supply. The influence has now weakened," Mattson said.
"It is yet to be seen how strong the trend of the last two months will be during the rest of the year," he added.
Cultor also said the clearance of its acquisition of Belgian chemical group Solvay's industrial enzymes unit in the U.S. had been "somewhat delayed".
To have a positive effect as soon as possible, the deal needed various arrangements to go through without delay and rationalisation to begin, it said.
Cultor said it had about 1,600 patents covering some 200 inventions, excluding its half-share in 500 patents owned by Genencor, which Cultor owns with Eastman Chemical Co of the U.S.
It said it was putting increasing resources in this field, and now has some 10 to 20 percent annual growth in its number of patent applications.
